name: Session Router QUIC Layer — Upstream Analysis
description: TRUG analysis of upstream session-router QUIC transport layer (src/link/). Three-pass graph: structural flow, internal state machines, per-section implementation details. Purpose: inform complete rewrite of Layer 4.

properties.name: QUIC Transport Layer
properties.description: Two classes + one struct. Endpoint owns QUIC connections and lifecycle. Manager owns command dispatch and protocol message handling. Connection wraps a quic::Connection + datagrams + control stream.

properties.name: Endpoint
properties.role: Owns the QUIC event loop, TLS credentials, connection maps, tickers, and all connection lifecycle logic. The core of the transport layer.

properties.name: Manager
properties.role: Command dispatch and protocol message handling. Registers BT stream handlers on control streams. Routes path_control, session_control, gossip_rc, fetch_rcs, publish_cc, find_cc. Bridges QUIC transport to protocol logic.

properties.name: Connection
properties.role: Simple wrapper: quic::Connection + datagrams handle + BTRequestStream control stream. close() delegates to conn->close_connection(errcode).

properties.name: Endpoint::Endpoint(Manager&)
properties.description: Constructs QUIC endpoint. Creates event loop, TLS creds (Ed25519 keys for relays, unauthenticated for clients), configures ALPNs, datagrams (2M queue, ACTIVE splitting), 0-RTT callbacks, key verification callback, and calls endpoint->listen().

properties.name: Connection Storage
properties.description: Six separate maps tracking connections by type, direction, and lifecycle state. This is the core data model.

properties.name: relay_conns
properties.description: Established relay-to-relay connections. relay_conn stores BOTH inbound and outbound with winner selection. Relay only.

properties.name: relay_bidir
properties.description: Tracks relays with BOTH directions connected. Value = timestamp when latest bidirectional connection stored. Used by redundancy ticker to know when REDUNDANT_LINGER has passed.

properties.name: pending_outbound
properties.description: Not-yet-established outbound connections. On establishment, moved to relay_conns (relays) or client_conns (clients). On failure, removed.

properties.name: pending_dead
properties.description: Dead/deregistered relay IDs with timestamp of when first noticed. After DEREGGED_LINGER (30min), connection closed. Can be 'resurrected' if relay re-registers.

properties.name: client_conns
properties.description: Established client-to-relay connections. Client only (outbound edge connections).

properties.name: inbound_clients
properties.description: Inbound client connections. Relay only. Keyed by QUIC ConnectionID (not RouterID, because clients may be unauthenticated).

properties.name: relay_conn struct
properties.description: Bidirectional connection pair. Stores inbound + outbound shared_ptr<Connection>. Winner determined by: inbound_wins = (their_rid < our_rid). set_conn() replaces direction and updates preferred conn pointer. close_redundant() closes the loser direction with CONN_CLOSE_REDUNDANT=6.

properties.name: Tickers
properties.description: Two periodic timers managing connection lifecycle. Relay only. Started via start_tickers().

properties.name: close_redundant()
properties.description: Iterates relay_bidir. For entries older than REDUNDANT_LINGER, calls relay_conn::close_redundant() which closes the loser direction (CONN_CLOSE_REDUNDANT=6). Removes from relay_bidir after closing.

properties.name: check_deregged_conns()
properties.description: Two phases: (1) Close connections to relays that have been dead > DEREGGED_LINGER (30min) — close_all, erase from relay_conns, pending_outbound, relay_bidir. Can resurrect if re-registered. (2) Scan relay_conns for newly unregistered relays, add to pending_dead with current timestamp.

properties.name: on_conn_established()
properties.description: QUIC callback when connection completes handshake. For inbound: creates control stream via make_control() BEFORE transferring to router loop (critical — stream must be queued before data arrives). Transfers to router._jq->call() then dispatches to on_inbound_conn() or on_outbound_conn(). Uses weak_from_this() to handle connection death during transfer.

properties.name: on_inbound_conn()
properties.description: Handles established inbound connections. Routes by ALPN: BOOTSTRAP_ALPN → log and return (untracked). RELAY_ALPN → create relay_conn with winner=(their_rid < our_rid), set_conn(inbound=true), add to relay_bidir if outbound exists. CLIENT_ALPN → store in inbound_clients by ConnectionID.

properties.name: on_outbound_conn()
properties.description: Handles established outbound connections. Moves from pending_outbound to: relay_conns (relay, set_conn outbound=false, add to relay_bidir if inbound exists) or client_conns (client). Calls router.on_edge_conn_change() for clients.

properties.name: on_conn_closed()
properties.description: QUIC callback when connection closes. Uses canary shared_ptr for lifetime safety — if Endpoint destroyed, early returns. Routes by ALPN: BOOTSTRAP → return (untracked). RELAY → find in relay_conns, match by reference_id to determine direction, close that direction, erase relay_conn if both gone, also check pending_outbound. CLIENT → relay: erase from inbound_clients. client: erase from client_conns. Empty ALPN (failed before negotiation) → erase from pending_outbound. Calls on_edge_conn_change() for clients.

properties.name: make_control()
properties.description: Creates BTRequestStream on a connection. Inbound: queue_incoming_stream (stream ID must be 0). Outbound: open_stream with stream_notify. Determines remote identity: RELAY_ALPN uses RouterID from key, others use ConnectionID. Calls manager.register_commands() (or register_bootstrap_commands for BOOTSTRAP_ALPN). Returns shared_ptr<BTRequestStream>.

properties.name: send_datagram()
properties.description: Two overloads: by RouterID (relay) or ConnectionID (client). Returns bool. Does NOT initiate new connections — drops if not connected. Uses get_relay_conn() or inbound_clients lookup. Checks is_stopping.

properties.name: send_command()
properties.description: Four overloads: by RelayContact, RouterID, ConnectionID, or variant. RelayContact version DOES initiate new connection via control_stream_for(). RouterID version looks up RC in NodeDB. ConnectionID version uses inbound_clients. All wrap response_handler to transfer execution to router loop. Returns bool (except RelayContact version returns void).

properties.name: ctrl_stream_impl()
properties.description: Core connection-or-create logic. If relay connected: return (true, existing control stream). If not: create in pending_outbound with endpoint->connect() + make_control(), return (false, new control stream). CRITICAL: this is where outbound connections are initiated. Sets keep_alive and idle_timeout based on is_service_node.

properties.name: bootstrap_connect() / testing_client_connect()
properties.description: Special untracked connections. Both use special_connect_impl() which: connects with no-creds, bootstrap idle timeout (10s), custom ALPN, own open/close callbacks (not the main ones). Returns (Connection, BTRequestStream) pair. NOT stored in any connection map. Short-lived, no keep-alive.

properties.name: shutdown()
properties.description: Ordered teardown: close_all on each relay_conn → clear relay_conns → clear relay_bidir → close each pending_outbound → close each client_conn → close each inbound_client → reset endpoint → reset loop. Order matters: connections must close before endpoint, endpoint before loop.

properties.name: Query functions
properties.description: get_relay_conn(), get_client_conn(), connected_to_relay(), get_current_relays(), num_relay_conns(), relay_connection_counts(), client_connection_counts(), unique_edge_range(), for_each_relay_conn(). Most use router._jq->call_get() for thread-safe access. for_each_relay_conn() asserts inside router loop.

properties.name: Key verification callback
properties.description: TLS client key verification. Non-relay ALPNs: accept if no key or valid size. RELAY_ALPN: MUST provide RouterID-sized key, must not be our own ID, must be registered in NodeDB. CRITICAL WARNING in code: must NOT call_get into router loop (deadlock risk — router call_gets into endpoint loop).

properties.name: 0-RTT callbacks
properties.description: Two callbacks registered on tls_creds. Store callback: on new 0-RTT ticket, store in NodeDB via store_0rtt(rid, data, expiry). Extract callback: on reconnect, retrieve from NodeDB via extract_0rtt(rid). Relay inbound: enable_inbound_0rtt(0s, 48h).

properties.name: register_commands()
properties.description: Registers BT stream handlers on control stream. ALL connections get: path_control, session_control. Relay-only additions: path_build, fetch_rcs, gossip_rc, publish_cc, find_cc, ping. ALL handlers transfer to router loop via router._jq->call(). WARNING in code: can be called from network OR router loop thread.

properties.name: register_bootstrap_commands()
properties.description: Registers single handler: bfetch_rcs. Bootstrap connections only support this one command. Server-side only (client doesn't register anything on bootstrap).

properties.name: gossip_rc() / handle_gossip_rc()
properties.description: RC propagation. gossip_rc() sends to all relay peers except origin and sender. handle_gossip_rc() validates incoming RC, verifies+stores via NodeDB, re-gossips if new/significantly updated.

properties.name: Path request handlers
properties.description: Six path request types routed via path_requests static map: publish_cc, find_cc, fetch_rcs, fetch_rids, resolve_sns, path_ping. Plus handle_path_build (path construction) and handle_path_latency.

properties.name: Session handlers
properties.description: handle_session_message() dispatches datagrams. handle_session_handshake() processes init/accept/switch. handle_session_data() and handle_session_control() handle payload decryption and routing. handle_path_session_control() bridges path to session.

properties.name: connect_to_keep_alive()
properties.description: Connects to N random relays from NodeDB, filtering out already-connected (including pending). Used to maintain relay mesh connectivity.

properties.name: stop()
properties.description: Sets is_stopping atomic flag (checked by send operations). Calls endpoint.shutdown() via router._jq->call_get() — synchronous, waits for completion. Destructor calls stop().
Manager contains Endpoint as member. Endpoint constructor takes Manager&.
Connection wraps quic::Connection + datagrams + control_stream. Stored in all connection maps.
Constructor registers key verify callback on tls_creds. Relay only.
Constructor registers 0-RTT store/extract callbacks. Both relay and client.
Inbound connections dispatched to on_inbound_conn() after router loop transfer.
Outbound connections dispatched to on_outbound_conn() after router loop transfer.
For inbound: make_control() called BEFORE router loop transfer (critical ordering).
RELAY_ALPN connections stored in relay_conns via relay_conn::set_conn(inbound=true).
If outbound already exists for this relay, adds to relay_bidir with current timestamp.
CLIENT_ALPN connections stored in inbound_clients by ConnectionID.
Finds and removes from pending_outbound.
Relay: stores in relay_conns via relay_conn::set_conn(inbound=false).
If inbound already exists, adds to relay_bidir.
Client: stores in client_conns.
RELAY_ALPN: finds by RouterID, matches direction by reference_id, closes direction. Erases relay_conn if both gone.
Erases from relay_bidir on any relay connection close.
Checks pending_outbound if not found in relay_conns (relay) or for empty-ALPN outbound (failed pre-negotiation).
CLIENT_ALPN on client: erases from client_conns, matching by reference_id.
CLIENT_ALPN on relay: erases from inbound_clients by ConnectionID.
Creates new connection in pending_outbound if not already connected or pending.
Creates control stream on new outbound connection.
Iterates relay_bidir, closes redundant for entries past REDUNDANT_LINGER.
Finds relay_conn to call close_redundant() on.
Checks timestamps, removes expired dead entries, adds newly unregistered relays.
Closes and erases connections to relays dead > DEREGGED_LINGER.
Also cleans pending connections to dead relays.
Erases bidir tracking for dead relays.
Registers protocol handlers on control stream. Non-bootstrap connections.
Registers bfetch_rcs handler on bootstrap connections. Server-side only.
RelayContact overload uses control_stream_for() which calls ctrl_stream_impl().
Shutdown closes all relay connections first.
Then pending outbound.
Then client connections.
Then inbound clients. Then endpoint. Then loop.
gossip_rc uses for_each_relay_conn + control_stream->command directly (no send_command wrapper).
Path handlers like publish_cc forward via endpoint.send_command().
Uses ensure_connection() which calls ctrl_stream_impl().
stop() calls endpoint.shutdown() via router._jq->call_get().

constants.REDUNDANT_LINGER: 20s — time before closing redundant bidirectional connection
constants.DEREGGED_LINGER: 30min — time before closing connection to deregistered relay
constants.CONN_CLOSE_REDUNDANT: 6 — error code for redundant connection close

threading_model.network_loop: quic::Loop — owns QUIC endpoint, runs callbacks. Endpoint.loop member.
threading_model.router_loop: router._jq (JobQueue) — owns all connection maps and protocol state.
threading_model.pattern: Callbacks fire in network loop → transfer to router loop via router._jq->call(). Query functions use router._jq->call_get() for synchronous reads.
threading_model.deadlock_risk: Key verify callback MUST NOT call_get into router loop (documented in code). Router frequently call_gets into endpoint loop. Bidirectional call_get = deadlock.
threading_model.canary: Endpoint destructor sets *canary = false. on_conn_closed lambda checks canary before accessing this. Prevents use-after-free during shutdown.

connection_lifecycle.outbound_relay: ctrl_stream_impl() creates in pending_outbound → on_conn_established() transfers to router loop → on_outbound_conn() moves to relay_conns + adds to relay_bidir if inbound exists → redundancy_ticker closes loser after REDUNDANT_LINGER
connection_lifecycle.inbound_relay: QUIC callback → on_conn_established() creates control stream FIRST then transfers → on_inbound_conn() creates relay_conn with winner=(their_rid < our_rid), stores inbound, adds to relay_bidir if outbound exists
connection_lifecycle.outbound_client: ctrl_stream_impl() creates in pending_outbound → on_outbound_conn() moves to client_conns → on_edge_conn_change()
connection_lifecycle.inbound_client: on_inbound_conn() stores in inbound_clients by ConnectionID
connection_lifecycle.bootstrap: special_connect_impl() — untracked, own callbacks, no keep_alive, 10s timeout, not stored in any map
connection_lifecycle.death: on_conn_closed routes by ALPN → cleans from appropriate map → erases relay_bidir → erases pending_outbound if present
connection_lifecycle.deregistration: check_deregged_conns() adds to pending_dead → 30min later closes and erases everything

Session_Router_R.commands: path_control, session_control, path_build, fetch_rcs, gossip_rc, publish_cc, find_cc, ping

winner_selection.symmetry: Both sides compute the same answer. If A < B: A's inbound (from B) wins on A's side, B's outbound (to A) wins on B's side → same physical connection wins on both sides.
winner_selection.timing: Winner takes effect immediately on set_conn(). Loser kept alive for REDUNDANT_LINGER (20s) to drain in-flight messages. Then closed with CONN_CLOSE_REDUNDANT=6.

critical_ordering.inbound_control_stream: make_control() MUST be called in network loop callback BEFORE transferring to router loop. If deferred, incoming stream data could arrive and create a plain Stream instead of BTRequestStream. This is the most subtle bug risk in the entire layer.
critical_ordering.shutdown_order: close connections → clear maps → reset endpoint → reset loop. Loop must outlive endpoint. Endpoint must outlive connections.

must_preserve: Six separate connection maps (not a flat map)
relay_conn bidirectional struct with winner selection
Key verification on relay ALPN (NodeDB registered check)
Canary or equivalent lifetime safety in callbacks
Control stream creation before router loop transfer (inbound)
Bootstrap connections untracked with own callbacks
Response handler wrapping for router loop transfer
can_simplify: Threading: Go goroutines + channels replace call_get/call pattern entirely
Canary: Go GC eliminates use-after-free concern
Connection struct: Go interface instead of shared_ptr wrapping
Static map of path_requests: Go function map or switch
